statement: C0044 is the fixed-direction annealed zero-one question P0(lim X_n dot ell=+infinity) in {0,1} for iid strictly elliptic nearest-neighbor transition rows on Z^d, d>=3, ell nonzero. Current openness is UNKNOWN because a newer public source claims a solution without a verified implementation receipt in this packet.

statement: For eta_n=T_Xn omega, under a stationary environment law P, mu_n=Law(eta_n) has density f_n(omega)=sum_x P_-x,omega(X_n=0); f_0=1 and f_(n+1)=sum_e omega(-e,e) f_n(T_-e omega). Each sum over x is finite and E_P f_n=1.
assumptions: Nearest-neighbor RWRE on Z^d; T_x omega(y,e)=omega(x+y,e); annealed walk starts at 0; P invariant under all lattice shifts.
proof_or_counterexample: Change variables by T_x in each endpoint term of E phi(T_Xn omega); translate the walk from 0 to -x. Full proof at L1.
remaining_gap: No mathematical gap in this authored lemma identified; independent audit pending. Finite-time absolute continuity supplies no uniform-integrability bound.

statement: For h(omega)=P_0,omega(Aell), h is R-harmonic. If 0<E_P h<1, then 0<h<1 P-almost surely.
assumptions: Stationary and ergodic P under the full Z^d shift group; strictly elliptic nearest-neighbor walk; nonzero fixed ell; Rphi=sum_e omega(0,e) phi(T_e omega); Aell={X_n dot ell tends to +infinity}.
proof_or_counterexample: Markov conditioning gives Rh=h. Strict positivity propagates zeros in both neighboring directions; {h=0} and {h=1} are invariant modulo null sets, and ergodicity excludes them under mixed expectation.
remaining_gap: No mathematical gap in this authored lemma identified; independent audit pending. Zero-set invariance is not invariance of h itself.

statement: With F_n containing the entire environment and path through time n, M_n=h(T_Xn omega)=E[1_Aell|F_n] tends to 1_Aell in L2. D_n=E[M_n(1-M_n)] tends to zero, and D_n=E_P[h(1-h)]-sum_(j<n) E[Gamma_h(eta_j)], with Gamma_h=sum_e omega(0,e)(h(T_e omega)-h(omega))^2.
assumptions: Setup of L2; full environment/path increasing filtration; directional escape unchanged by any finite prefix and spatial displacement.
proof_or_counterexample: Conditional Markov property and upward conditional-expectation convergence; martingale square increments telescope. Orthogonality uses the named filtration, not independent increments. The initial energy is E_P h(1-h), not p(1-p).
remaining_gap: No mathematical gap in this authored lemma identified; independent audit pending. Does not compare mu_n with P uniformly.

statement: The directional annealed probability is zero or one if the finite-time densities f_n, or the Cesaro densities bar_f_N, have a uniformly integrable subsequence whose times tend to infinity. A uniformly bounded Lr norm for any r>1 or relative entropy on that subsequence is sufficient.
assumptions: Stationary ergodic strictly elliptic nearest-neighbor P and fixed nonzero ell; f_n is defined in L1; bar_f_N=N^-1 sum_(n<N) f_n; uniform integrability is with respect to P.
proof_or_counterexample: Under a mixed probability u=h(1-h)>0 P-a.s.; mu_n(u) and bar_mu_N(u) tend to zero. The densities therefore put mass at least 1-a/t on {u<=t}, whose P-mass tends to zero, contradicting UI.
remaining_gap: GAP-G1: IID and strict ellipticity alone have not been shown to provide such a subsequence. This is a sufficient condition, not an equivalence.

statement: Under 0<p=P0(Aell)<1, for g=f_n or bar_f_N, a=integral h(1-h)g dP, delta_t=P(h(1-h)<=t), b=(1-a/t)_+, r>1, and 0<delta_t<1: ||g||r>=b delta_t^(-(1-1/r)) and integral g log g dP>=b log(1/delta_t)-log 2. Thus every Lr norm and both entropies diverge as n or N tends to infinity.
assumptions: Stationary ergodic strictly elliptic nearest-neighbor P, fixed nonzero ell, mixed annealed probability; finite-time and Cesaro densities from L1; natural logarithm and 0 log 0=0.
proof_or_counterexample: Mass concentration from L3, Holder on the low-uncertainty set, and two-set Jensen for relative entropy. Choose t first, then a sufficiently large time; delta_t>0 follows from D_n tending to zero.
remaining_gap: Independent audit pending. GAP-G1 remains: exclude this concentration under arbitrary IID rows. No parent theorem follows without this missing step.

statement: The directional zero-one law holds for a stationary ergodic strictly elliptic nearest-neighbor environment satisfying sum_e omega(-e,e)=1 P-a.s., since this makes P invariant for the environment kernel and f_n identically one.
assumptions: The incoming-probability sum condition is additional to stationary ergodicity and strict ellipticity; fixed nonzero direction. Under IID this extra condition forces deterministic rows.
proof_or_counterexample: Stationarity turns integral Rphi into integral phi sum_e omega(-e,e). Apply L4 to f_n=1. Under IID, the incoming summands are bounded independent variables with deterministic sum; their variances vanish.
remaining_gap: Independent audit pending. This extra hypothesis is not supplied by the original target assumptions.

statement: The proposed full-proof step would require excluding concentration of reverse environment densities on arbitrarily small-P sets of low directional uncertainty under general IID strict ellipticity.
assumptions: Original strict-elliptic IID C0044 setup; finite-time formulas alone are available; no invariant ac law, finite regeneration mean or local measurability of h is assumed.
proof_or_counterexample: The implication from IID to a UI subsequence is not proved. Compactness and finite-time absolute continuity do not fill it.
remaining_gap: GAP-G1 is open in this attempt and is the only load-bearing step between the restricted UI theorem and C0044.
